title: Riley 1946
text:
\[
\frac{\mathrm{d} P}{\mathrm{d} t } = (\overline{P_h} - R - G)~P
\]
, where \(P\) is the phytoplankton biomass, \(\overline{P_h}\) is the average photosynthesis in euphotic zone, and \(G\) is the grazing rate.



The biomass-specific photosynthesis rate \(\overline{P_h}\) is calculated as
\[
\overline{P_h}  = \frac{\textcolor{#B3541E}{p}~\textcolor{#2B5F9E}{I_0}}{\textcolor{#2B5F9E}{k~z_\text{euph}}}~(1-\mathrm{e}^{-\textcolor{#2B5F9E}{k~z_\text{euph}}})~\textcolor{#2B5F9E}{L_\text{N}~L_\text{V}}
\]
Parameters are shown in red and forcing variables in blue
Parameters:

\(\textcolor{#B3541E}{p}\) = 2.5 \(\mathrm{gC~(gC)^{-1}~d^{-1}(g~cal~cm^{-2}~min^{-1}})^{-1}\) Photosynthetic rate per unit irradiance

Forcing variables:

\(\textcolor{#2B5F9E}{I_0}\): Light intensity at sea surface in \(\mathrm{\mu E~m^{-2}~s^{-1}}\)
\(\textcolor{#2B5F9E}{k}\): Light attenuation in the euphotic zone in \(\mathrm{m^{-1}}\)
\(\textcolor{#2B5F9E}{L_\text{N}}\): Limiting effects due to nutrients, unitless
\(\textcolor{#2B5F9E}{L_\text{V}}\): Limiting effects due to turbulence, unitless
\(\textcolor{#2B5F9E}{z_\text{euph}}\): Depth of the euphotic zone in \(\mathrm{m}\)

\(\textcolor{#2B5F9E}{L_\text{V}}\) is calculated as
\[
\textcolor{#2B5F9E}{L_\text{V}} = \min(1, \frac{\textcolor{#2B5F9E}{z_\text{euph}}}{\textcolor{#2B5F9E}{z_\text{mix}}})
\] , where \(\textcolor{#2B5F9E}{z_\text{mix}}\) is the depth of the mixed layer in \(\mathrm{m}\)
\(\textcolor{#2B5F9E}{z_\text{euph}}\) is calculated as
\[
\textcolor{#2B5F9E}{z_\text{euph}} = \frac{\log(\frac{\textcolor{#2B5F9E}{I_0}}{\textcolor{#B3541E}{I_\text{min}}})}{\textcolor{#2B5F9E}{k}}
\] , where \(\textcolor{#B3541E}{I_\text{min}}\) is a parameter defining the light intensity at the base of the euphotic zone: 0.0015 \(\mathrm{g~cal~cm^{−2}~min^{−1}}\)



The biomass-specific respiration rate \(R\) is calculated as
\[
R = \textcolor{#B3541E}{R_0}~\mathrm{e}^{\textcolor{#B3541E}{r}~\textcolor{#2B5F9E}{\text{temp}}}
\]
Parameters:

\(\textcolor{#B3541E}{R_0}\): 0.0175 \(\text{d}^{-1}\) Respiration rate of phytoplankton at 0 °C
\(\textcolor{#B3541E}{r}\): 0.069 \(\text{°C}^{-1}\) Temperature dependency of respiration rate

\(\textcolor{#B3541E}{r}\), corresponds to \(Q_{10} = 2\), i.e. doubling of rate for 10 °C increase in temperature: \(\mathrm{e}^{10 \text{°C}~0.069~\textrm{°C}^{-1}}\approx2\)
Forcing Variables:

\(\textcolor{#2B5F9E}{\text{temp}}\): Sea-surface (?) temperature in \(\textrm{°C}\)




The biomass-specific grazing rate \(G\) is calculated as
\[
G = \textcolor{#B3541E}{g}~\textcolor{#2B5F9E}{zoo_{\text{bm}}}
\]
Parameters:

\(\textcolor{#B3541E}{g}\): 0.0075 \(\mathrm{d^{-1}(gC~m^{-2}})^{-1}\) Clearance rate of grazers

Forcing Variables:

\(\textcolor{#2B5F9E}{zoo_{\text{bm}}}\): Zooplankton biomass in \(\mathrm{gC~m^{-2}}\) (?)

title: Riley 1946
text:
Model in R
Setup
Load packages


Code
library(here)
library(deSolve)
library(patchwork)
library(mgcv)
require(ecolMod)
library(lhs)
library(ggh4x)
library(tidyverse)


Load forcing and observed data


Code
dat_forc <- read.csv(here("data", "forcing.csv")) %>%
  mutate(days = days + 1) # data is 0 base (1.1. corresponds to day 0)

dat_obs <- read.csv(here("data", "observed.csv"))


Define parameters

parameters <- c(
  p = 2.5,
  I_min = 0.0015,
  r = 0.069,
  R_0 = 0.0175,
  g = 0.0075
)

Define first model version. Use approx() to interpolate forcing data for each time point. For now, use rule = 2 so that, outside the forcing-data range, boundary values are returned.

m_riley <- function(time, state, parameters, forcing_tbl) {
  with(as.list(c(state, parameters)), {
    # helper function to interpolate frocing data
    get_approx <- function(var) {
      approx(
        x = forcing_tbl$days,
        y = forcing_tbl[[var]],
        xout = time,
        rule = 2
      )$y
    }

    # interpolate at "time"
    I_0_t <- max(get_approx("I_0"), I_min * 1.0001) #  avoid I_0 < I_min which would lead to division by 0 (z_eup => 0, used in photos equation)
    k_t <- max(get_approx("k"), 1e-6) # avoid possible 0-division in z_euph formula
    L_N_t <- get_approx("L_N")
    z_mix_t <- get_approx("z_mix")
    temp_t <- get_approx("temp")
    zoo_bm_t <- get_approx("zoo_bm")

    # Euphotic depth
    z_euph <- log(I_0_t / I_min) / k_t

    # Light limitation
    L_V <- if (z_euph < z_mix_t) z_euph / z_mix_t else 1

    photos <- (p * I_0_t) /
      (k_t * z_euph) *
      (1 - exp(-k_t * z_euph)) *
      L_N_t *
      L_V

    resp <- R_0 * exp(r * temp_t)
    graz <- g * zoo_bm_t

    dPhyto_bm <- (photos - resp - graz) * Phyto_bm

    list(
      dPhyto_bm,
      photos = photos,
      resp = resp,
      graz = graz
    )
  })
}

Define initial conditions

state <- c(Phyto_bm = 3.377)

Time period to be integrated. Use -15 days because starting value is one time step (originally 15 days) before start of model.

approx() will use the 1st forcing data point for -15 days. See below for an alternative. Use interval of 1 day instead of 15 days.


times <- seq(-15, 365, 1)

Run the model (passing dat_forc in ...)

solution <- ode(
  y = state,
  times = times,
  func = m_riley,
  parms = parameters,
  forcing_tbl = dat_forc
)

Plot the integrated data


Code
plot_phytop <- solution %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  filter(time > 0) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = time, y = Phyto_bm)) +
  geom_area(fill = "lightblue") +
  geom_point(data = dat_obs) +
  labs(x = "Days", y = expression("Phytoplankton biomass (gC " * m^-2 * ")")) +
  theme_light()










Figure 1: Modelled phytoplankton biomass





Plot the rates


Code
# ggplot() can’t make stacked area plots like Excel. geom_ribbon with the explicit values have to be used.
plot_rates <- solution %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  filter(time > 0) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = time)) +
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(
      ymin = photos - resp,
      ymax = photos,
      fill = "Respiration"
    )
  ) +
  # green: respiration→net layer
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(
      ymin = photos - resp - graz,
      ymax = photos - resp,
      fill = "Grazing"
    )
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    name = NULL,
    values = c(
      "Respiration" = "#5095d4",
      "Grazing" = "#125a52"
    )
  ) +
  geom_line(
    aes(y = photos - resp - graz, linetype = "Net Production"),
    linewidth = .7
  ) +
  geom_line(
    aes(y = photos, linetype = "Gross Production"),
    linewidth = .7
  ) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "11", col = "grey30") +
  scale_linetype_manual(
    name = NULL,
    values = c("Net Production" = "solid", "Gross Production" = "11")
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Days",
    y = expression(
      "Specific rate (d"^{
        -1
      } *
        ")"
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  theme_light() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
plot_rates








Figure 2: Modelled production rates

title: Riley 1946
text:
GAMs to interpolate forcing
As seen in Figure 2, some predictions are quite ‘jaggy’. This is probably due to the linear approximations used for the forcing variables. Additionally, using the next value for timepoints outside of the range of the forcing data set (start = -15 days, end = 365 days) is not ideal.
As an alternative, use “cyclic” GAMs, meaning the first values are considered when fitting the end of the 365-day period.
Although GAMs are fitted only once outside of the model function, the prediction step takes much more time than approx().
Fit a GAM for each parameter:

gam_list <- list()
vars <- c("I_0", "k", "L_N", "z_mix", "temp", "zoo_bm")

for (v in vars) {
  form <- bquote(.(as.name(v)) ~ s(days, k = .(nrow(dat_forc)), bs = "cc"))
  gam_list[[v]] <- gam(
    formula = form,
    data = dat_forc,
    family = Gamma(link = "log"),
    method = "REML",
    knots = list(days = c(0, 365))
  )
}

Update model code


Code
m_riley_g <- function(time, state, parameters, gam_list_m) {
  with(as.list(c(state, parameters)), {
    # helper function to predict data with GAMs
    get_predict <- function(parameter) {
      predict(gam_list_m[[parameter]], newdata = data.frame(days = time)) %>%
        # log link was used, predictions on log scale
        exp()
    }

    I_0_t <- max(get_predict("I_0"), I_min * 1.0001) #  avoid I_0 < I_min which would lead to division by 0 (z_eup => 0, used in photos equation)
    k_t <- max(get_predict("k"), 1e-6) # avoid possibel 0 division in z_euph formula
    L_N_t <- min(c(1, get_predict("L_N"))) # could potentially exceed 1
    z_mix_t <- get_predict("z_mix")
    temp_t <- get_predict("temp")
    zoo_bm_t <- get_predict("zoo_bm")

    # Euphotic depth
    z_euph <- log(I_0_t / I_min) / k_t

    # Light limitation
    L_V <- if (z_euph < z_mix_t) z_euph / z_mix_t else 1

    photos <- (p * I_0_t) /
      (k_t * z_euph) *
      (1 - exp(-k_t * z_euph)) *
      L_N_t *
      L_V

    resp <- R_0 * exp(r * temp_t)
    graz <- g * zoo_bm_t

    dPhyto_bm <- (photos - resp - graz) * Phyto_bm

    list(
      dPhyto_bm,
      photos = photos,
      resp = resp,
      graz = graz
    )
  })
}


Now, solve as before

Takes a while to fit, not evaluated after 1st run, but saved to output folder


solution_g <- ode(
  y = state,
  times = times,
  func = m_riley_g,
  parms = parameters,
  gam_list_m = gam_list
)

write_rds(solution_g, here("output", "solution_g.rds"))

Read solution_g


Code
solution_g <- readRDS(here("output", "solution_g.rds"))

Plot both interpolation methods for the forcing data


Code
dat_forc_long <- dat_forc %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(vars), names_to = "variable", values_to = "value")

dat_interp_forc <- data.frame(days = seq(1, 365))

# interpolate forcing data for each variable as within the model formula
# loop over "vars" which contail the variable names of the forcing data

dat_interp_forc <- bind_rows(
  map(vars, function(v) {
    tibble(
      days = dat_interp_forc$days,

title: Riley 1946
text:
Calibration
To improve the fit toward the end of the simulation, copy the first observed data point (day 8) to day 365.


Code
dat_obs <- dat_obs %>%
  add_row(time = 365, Phyto_bm = dat_obs$Phyto_bm[1])


This step takes some time, use the faster model with approx(). Only integrate at -15 days (initial conditions) and the timpoints in observed data. It still takes a long time to fit, so save output after first run.
The lower bound is 0.5 × the baseline parameter value, and the upper bound is 2 × the baseline value.

times_calib <- c(-15, dat_obs$time)

# lower parameters
par_lower <- parameters * 0.5

# upper parameters
par_upper <- parameters * 2

# cost function returns sums of squared
cost_price <- function(par_vec, obs = dat_obs) {
  progress <<- ifelse(exists("progress"), progress + 1, 1)
  if (progress %% 100 == 0) {
    cat(progress, "evaluations\n")
  }
  # integrate as before, using par_vec as parameter input
  sim <- tryCatch(
    ode(
      y = state,
      times = times_calib,
      func = m_riley,
      parms = as.list(par_vec),
      forcing_tbl = dat_forc
    ),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )

  # if ode() fails, return huge penalty value
  if (is.null(sim)) {
    return(1e8)
  }

  # subset simulations to timpoints in observed data (= remove -15 days)
  sim_match <- sim[sim[, "time"] %in% obs$time, "Phyto_bm"]

  # check for non-finite values
  if (any(!is.finite(sim_match))) {
    return(1e8)
  }

  # sum of squared residuals
  sum((sim_match - obs$Phyto_bm)^2)
}


fit_price <- pricefit(
  par = parameters,
  minpar = par_lower,
  maxpar = par_upper,
  func = cost_price,
  npop = 50,
  numiter = 10000,
  varleft = 1e-8,
  centroid = 3
)


write_rds(fit_price, here("output", "fit_price.rds"))

Read output, use for new integration, and plot


Code
fit_price <- readRDS(here("output", "fit_price.rds"))

solution_price <- ode(
  y = state,
  times = times,
  func = m_riley,
  parms = fit_price$par,
  forcing_tbl = dat_forc
)

solution %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  select(time, original = Phyto_bm) %>%
  left_join(
    solution_price %>%
      as.data.frame() %>%
      select(time, pricefit = Phyto_bm),
    by = "time"
  ) %>%
  filter(time > 0) %>%
  pivot_longer(original:pricefit) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = time)) +
  geom_line(aes(col = name, y = value)) +
  geom_point(data = dat_obs, aes(y = Phyto_bm)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#be5523", "#a7a8ec")) +
  labs(
    x = "Days",
    y = expression("Phytoplankton biomass (gC " * m^-2 * ")"),
    col = NULL

Sensitivity Analysis

Local
Get custom function to local sensitivity analysis. For each parameter, it plots the “baseline” value, and the scenario if that baseline value is multiplied by 0.8 and 1.2 (or other values).

source(here("scripts", "plot_local_sensitivity.R"))

(plot_parameter_effect(par_name = "p") +

    plot_layout(axes = "collect")) +
